items.p: The fifth rise of 2026, on a 6–3 vote, with inflation at 4.3%. No cut is expected before 2028.
items.x: Lower borrowing capacity for every buyer. Both cities' 2027 base cases are negative.

items.h: Perth −1.7% in October, −5.7% over the quarter
items.p: National values have fallen for seven months straight. Capital cities are down 8.1% since March, the fastest fall in 40 years of data.
items.x: Perth base case set at −6% for 2027 and −2% for 2028. The Perth correction is already underway.

items.h: Buyer's market: 39 days on market, 4.7% discounting
items.p: Advertised stock is the highest for this time of year since 2019. Auction clearance rates are below 50%.
items.x: Good for you as a buyer. Offer below asking price, and expect the medians shown here to be beatable.

items.h: Budget limits negative gearing and changes CGT
items.p: From July 2027, negative gearing for future purchases applies to new builds only, and the 50% CGT discount is replaced by indexation. The ATO says this is not yet law, so check its current status.
items.x: Fewer investors bidding on established entry-level houses, which helps first home buyers.

items.h: Melton line electrification: $152.7m for planning only
items.p: Design and approvals run to mid-2027, with no construction date. Separately, $14.8m funds longer trains on the Wyndham Vale line.
items.x: Not in the model. Real upside for Melton and Wyndham Vale if construction is funded.

items.p: The Coalition has promised 25 hybrid trains for the Melton and Wyndham Vale lines. Rail and housing commitments could change after the vote.
items.x: Watch it. A funded rail commitment for the west would raise Melton and Wyndham Vale tilts.

items.h: WA first home buyer exemption raised to $600k
items.p: This matches Victoria. At $600k you pay $0 duty in either state. Above that, the concession runs to $800k in WA and $750k in Victoria.
items.x: Removes stamp duty from the decision at your budget.

items.p: Domain: Melbourne houses −4% to −8%, Perth +5% to +9% for the year to June 2027. ANZ: Perth −3.1% in 2027.
items.x: Our Perth base case is more bearish than Domain's and close to ANZ's. Use the Bull button if you side with Domain.

items.h: Perth still has the tightest rentals
items.p: Vacancy is about 0.6%, and WA has the strongest interstate migration of any state. Melbourne vacancy is 1.4–1.6%.
items.x: This keeps Perth's bear case from going deeper than about −16% to −25% in the most stretched suburbs.

items.p: A few lenders are offering 5.89–6.13% for owner-occupiers. The big four banks charge more.
items.x: The planner defaults to 6.20%. Each extra 0.25% adds about $70 a month on a $475k loan.
